title: Which of these numbers do two and five divide?
description: Three thousand seven hundred sixteen and four thousand seventy five are written as sums of place values to test divisibility by two and by five. Keeko's doubt is that four thousand seventy five is divisible by two, because it starts with an even digit.
teaching_notes: One idea: all the places except the units place are multiples of ten, so the units digit alone decides divisibility by two and by five. Watch for students who look at the first digit, or any even digit, instead of the units digit.

source: Use place values to decide whether 3716 and 4075 are divisib
video_script.why: The student has seen that only the units digit decides divisibility by ten and now uses the same idea for two and for five.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as a sum of place values, set aside the terms that are multiples of ten, and test only the units digit.
video_script.anchor: a chart of place values with the digits of the number in its boxes, as the book writes a number as thousands, hundreds, tens and units
video_script.wrong_answer: four thousand seventy five is divisible by two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko looks at the first digit, four, which is even, and forgets that only the units digit decides divisibility by two.
video_script.payoff_line: Three thousand seven hundred sixteen is divisible by two only

final_answer.value: 3716 is divisible by 2 only; 4075 is divisible by 5 only
final_answer.spoken: three thousand seven hundred sixteen is divisible by two only, and four thousand seventy five is divisible by five only

maths_rules: 3 x 1000, 7 x 100 and 1 x 10 are multiples of 10, so two and five divide them; 6 is left to test
6 is even but not 0 or 5, so 3716 is divisible by 2 and not by 5
4 x 1000, 0 x 100 and 7 x 10 are multiples of 10; 5 is left to test
5 is a multiple of 5 but odd, so 4075 is divisible by 5 and not by 2
video_script.design: One place-value chart for each number. The thousands, hundreds and tens boxes are set aside as multiples of ten, and the units digit is tested for two and for five.

<bookmark mark='nums'/>Look at three thousand seven hundred sixteen and four thousand seventy five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is each one divisible by two, or by five, and how can we tell?

<bookmark mark='ten'/>All of them except the units place are multiples of ten.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Ten is divisible by two and by five, so only the units digit is left to test.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers three thousand seven hundred sixteen and four thousand seventy five.

beats.on_screen: To find: is each number divisible by 2 or by 5?

marks.find: the question to settle is written

marks.write: three thousand seven hundred sixteen is written as a sum of place values

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write three thousand seven hundred sixteen as a sum of place values.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>It is three times one thousand, plus seven times one hundred, plus one times ten, plus six.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 3 x 1000, 7 x 100 and 1 x 10 are multiples of 10; 6 is even but not 0 or 5; divisible by 2, not by 5

marks.rest: the first three terms are marked as multiples of ten
marks.six: the units digit six is circled
marks.result: a tick is put beside divisible by 2 and a cross beside divisible by 5

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step two, test each term. The first three are multiples of ten, so two and five both divide them.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Only the units digit, six, is left. Six is even, but not zero or five.
<bookmark mark='result'/>That makes three thousand seven hundred sixteen divisible by two but not by five.

marks.write: four thousand seventy five is written as a sum of place values
marks.parts: the four terms of the sum appear one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step three, write four thousand seventy five the same way.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>It is four times one thousand, plus zero times one hundred, plus seven times ten, plus five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 4 x 1000, 0 x 100 and 7 x 10 are multiples of 10; 5 is a multiple of 5 but odd; divisible by 5, not by 2

marks.rest: the first three terms are marked as multiples of ten
marks.five: the units digit five is circled
marks.result: a tick is put beside divisible by 5 and a cross beside divisible by 2

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Again, the first three terms are multiples of ten.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Only the units digit, five, is left. Five is a multiple of five, but it is odd.
<bookmark mark='result'/>That makes four thousand seventy five divisible by five but not by two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3716 is divisible by 2 only; 4075 is divisible by 5 only
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three thousand seven hundred sixteen is divisible by two only.
Four thousand seventy five is divisible by five only.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the first digit four of four thousand seventy five
marks.thousands: the thousands box is shown as a multiple of ten

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four thousand seventy five is divisible by two, because it starts with an even digit.
<bookmark mark='thousands'/>Four thousands are a multiple of ten, so the first digit cannot decide.
<bookmark mark='units'/>The units digit is five, which is odd, so two does not divide it.
